title: A bone that may be broken — hold it still
applies_to: A limb that is painful, swollen, bent the wrong way, or cannot take any weight after a fall or a blow.

citations.source: WHO and IFRC International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines 2020
European Resuscitation Council Guidelines 2021: First Aid

steps.text: Ask where it hurts. Look at the shape of the limb and compare it with the other side.
Tell them to keep still. Support the limb with your hands in whatever position they are already holding it.
Call for an ambulance if the limb is bent the wrong way, if bone is showing, or if they cannot move or feel the hand or the foot.
If there is a wound, press a clean cloth around it, not down on the bone.
Pad around the limb with folded cloth or a rolled blanket so it cannot move.
For an arm, a sling made from a scarf can hold it against the chest. For a leg, pad both sides and leave it lying flat.
Put something cold, wrapped in cloth, over the swelling for up to 20 minutes.
Check the fingers or the toes every few minutes. They should stay warm and pink, and they should still feel your touch.
Get them to a clinic for any bone you think may be broken, even a small one in a finger or a toe.

do_not: Do not try to straighten the limb, and do not push a bone back in.
Do not give them anything to eat or drink, in case the hospital needs to put them to sleep.
Do not tie anything tightly around the limb. Tight binding cuts off the blood.
Do not let them walk on a leg you think is broken.
Do not put ice straight onto bare skin.
escalate_if: The hand or foot below the injury goes white, blue, cold, or numb — loosen everything and call now.
It is the neck, the back, the hip, or the thigh — do not move them at all, and wait for the crew.
Bone is through the skin, or the wound will not stop bleeding — call for an ambulance.
They fell from higher than their own height, or a vehicle hit them — call an ambulance even if they say they are fine.
The limb is swelling fast and the pain is getting much worse — that needs a hospital today.
